decision: compare backend only: Rust/tokio proxy core + Topcoat web layer serving the unchanged Go UI

decision: measure in OrbStack arm64 VM with the proxy capped at 1 CPU and 256 MiB, then check idle RSS on the Pi

decision: chain the temporary Pi add-on to the Go proxy on 18899 instead of EW11

decision: recorded 60 s of live bus traffic from the Go proxy as a read-only TCP client
why: replay real chunk sizes and timing instead of guessing

decision: spawned a Topcoat spike before any port work
why: riskiest unknowns first: raw static paths, SSE, WS, headers, arm64 musl build

decision: black-box contract suite over HTTP, WS, SSE, and TCP with Go as the oracle, both auth modes
why: the Rust side must match what the UI and clients observe, not Go internals
evidence: bench/contract/contract.mjs; my rerun against Go: RESULT 42 passed, 0 failed

decision: go: build the backend on Topcoat 0.11 with embedded static files via include_dir at original URLs
why: spike served all 18 UI files byte-identical, SSE, WS with same-origin policy matching Go, JSON, headers, cookies, two listeners on one runtime
result: GO; idle-ish RSS 2096 kB, 3.0 MB stripped binary, one run

decision: dry run of all four scenarios against Go, one run each
why: check the harness counts work and errors before trusting numbers
evidence: bench/results/20261101-223626: real delivered 6122 B and 301 WS logs = capture; stress 1.5M records, 0 gaps

decision: added a go-tuned side: same Go code with linear hex formatting in LogPacket
why: Go flood sat at 98% CPU and 3.7 MB/s; the per-byte string += in LogPacket is quadratic on 4096-byte reads, so Go as shipped is untuned there

decision: flood generator rewritten to send a prebuilt block
why: go-tuned flood ran at 72% proxy CPU, so the Python generator packing records one by one was the likely limiter

decision: accepted the Rust port after my own contract rerun in a linux/arm64 container: 42/42 for Go and Rust
why: the contract is the gate, not the agent's summary

decision: reformatted the port with rustfmt
why: the agent packed handlers into 200+ character lines; reviewers could not check the same-work rule

decision: made the quadratic hex formatting a default and added a linear-hex feature, mirroring go vs go-tuned
why: the agent copied Go's per-byte string rebuild on purpose; four sides separate language cost from that one hot spot
result: sides: go, go-tuned, rs, rs-tuned, rs-tuned-mi

decision: switched Rust credential checks to constant-time comparison like Go
why: agent flagged plain == as a difference from Go

decision: rebuilt rs, rs-tuned, rs-tuned-mi and reran the contract after my edits
why: my edits touched auth and formatting
evidence: contract: 42/42 for all three; shasum differs per variant

decision: drove the unchanged UI against the Rust backend in Chromium
why: contract checks the API; the UI is the real consumer
evidence: status card Connected, live logs, inspector rows, frame rule split 7+14, UI inject row 'Client -> UP 2 ca fe'

decision: started the full run: 5 sides x 4 scenarios x 5 runs, side order rotated each run, proxy capped at 1 CPU and 256 MiB
why: benchmark checklist: at least 5 alternating runs per side so drift favors none

decision: installed two temporary local add-ons on the Pi, Go and Rust, both chained to the production proxy on 18899 with auth on
why: same setup on both sides for an apples-to-apples idle and real-traffic check without touching EW11
evidence: /addons/stp_go_bench, /addons/stp_rs_bench; production log shows client#3 and client#4 from 127.0.0.1
result: sampling ha apps stats for 12 min

decision: measured both temporary add-ons on the Pi for ~10 min with real bus traffic and no clients
why: user asked for an on-device idle check; one window per side, so a ballpark
evidence: bench/results/pi-stats.jsonl: memory median Go 4820 KiB vs Rust 1152 KiB; CPU 1.75 s vs 0.95 s over the window

decision: uninstalled both temporary add-ons and deleted /addons/stp_*_bench
why: leave production as it was
evidence: ha apps list shows 0 stp_ add-ons; production status Connected, 1 client; 15 Kyungdong entities unchanged, 0 unavailable

decision: full run finished; real and stress show 0 WebSocket log messages for every Rust side
why: did-it-happen check: a missing count can mean missing work, which would make Rust CPU look better than it is
result: NOT VERIFIED for real and stress

decision: found the cause: Rust serializes {data,type} with sorted keys and loadgen only looked for type in the first 20 characters; fixed loadgen to parse JSON and count [PKT] log messages
why: the proxy did send the messages; the counter was wrong
evidence: manual WS read of rs-tuned: {"data":...,"type":"log"}; bench/loadgen.py

decision: rerun of real and stress with the fixed counter, 5 runs per side, side order rotated
why: the first run's Rust WebSocket counts were unverified
evidence: bench/results/20261102-003511/summary.md: real 301 WS logs on every side; stress ~10-13k on Rust

decision: noted that Go closed the WebSocket client in 3 of 10 stress runs (ConnectionClosedError, 0 messages), Rust never did
why: a closed WS client means Go skipped WS fan-out in those runs, so Go stress CPU may be slightly understated
evidence: raw.jsonl rows go stress run 2,3 and go-tuned stress run 1

decision: found a Rust shutdown hang: SIGTERM sent right after the web port opens is lost and the process never exits
why: startup timing script hung; gdb showed main parked in block_on after SIGTERM, and the handler was installed after the ports opened
evidence: gdb backtrace main.rs:76 block_on park; rs-mi-dbg 13/30 hangs

decision: moved SIGTERM registration to the top of main, before any port opens
why: a client that sees the port can no longer race the handler install
result: fixed; hot path unchanged, throughput runs used pre-fix binaries

decision: perf record segfaulted in the OrbStack VM, so I explained stress CPU with user vs kernel ticks and strace -c instead
why: need a named limiter, not a guess
result: both sides spend most CPU in socket writes; Go adds ~13k futex and ~6k nanosleep calls per 10 s

decision: first strace for Rust showed no client writes; the trace window started after the load generator stopped, so I lengthened the load to 60 s and reran
why: a profile of idle traffic would explain nothing

decision: re-measured startup with the fixed binaries, 15 alternating runs per side inside a 1-CPU container
why: docker-exec health polling made startup_s in run.py mostly Docker noise
evidence: bench/results/startup.json: go 8.1 ms, rs 2.4 ms median, 0 SIGTERM hangs
